problems.title: UAV Wing — Abrupt Stall
problems.bottleneck:
You are designing a fixed-wing UAV using a NACA 2412 airfoil. At cruise (Re = 500,000, α = 4°) it achieves CL = 0.8 — acceptable. But at α = 12° it stalls abruptly, making recovery unpredictable and unsafe.

Your constraint: cruise CL must stay above 0.75. Find a geometry modification that smooths the stall without sacrificing cruise performance.
problems.hint: Increasing camber delays separation — try the 6-series NACA family.

problems.title: Regional Transport — Symmetric Airfoil Penalty
problems.bottleneck:
A regional transport wing section uses a NACA 0015 symmetric airfoil inherited from an older design. At cruise conditions (Re = 1,500,000, α = 4°) it achieves L/D = 62 and CL = 0.42 — both below targets. The aerodynamics team needs L/D > 90 and CL > 0.6 simultaneously to meet range and payload requirements.

Constraint: the solution must work at α = 4° without modification to the cruise angle. Find the airfoil geometry that closes both gaps at once.
problems.hint: Symmetric airfoils generate less lift per unit drag than cambered ones at the same angle.

problems.title: Micro-UAV — Low Reynolds Dual Constraint
problems.bottleneck:
A micro-UAV wing operates deep in the low Reynolds number regime (Re = 100,000) where laminar separation bubbles dominate and conventional design intuition breaks down. The current NACA 0012 achieves L/D = 25 and CL = 0.65 at the design point (α = 6°).

The mission requires simultaneously: L/D > 20 to meet endurance targets AND CL > 0.8 to maintain level flight at low speed. These constraints conflict — increasing camber raises CL but drag rises steeply at low Re.

Find the airfoil geometry that satisfies both constraints at Re = 100,000, α = 6°.
problems.hint: At low Reynolds numbers, thin highly-cambered airfoils outperform thick ones — conventional wisdom reverses.
